_doc: Golden-corpus evaluation set for the always-on, offline rule-based extractor
(daemon/src/extract/rules.rs). Each case pairs an input chunk with the atomic
units a human judges USABLE for that text. The eval (tests/extraction_quality.rs)
runs extract_units() over every input and scores:
precision = usable_produced / produced   (the automatable analogue of the
write-up's Phase-1 '>=70% of sampled units judged usable' gate)
recall    = matched_expected / expected  (coverage; low by design, since the
rules are high-precision/low-recall and Ollama supplements them)
The gate asserts precision only. Inputs deliberately include noise (should
produce nothing), adversarial over-matches (produce an UNUSABLE unit -> lowers
precision), and facts the rules cannot catch (lower recall). Statements are the
full sentence as the extractor renders it (tidied, trailing . ! ? stripped).
A unit matches a label on (kind, statement, subject): subject is part of the
key because persistence resolves it into subject_entity_id and hangs graph
edges off it. Matching normalizes case/whitespace so wording just has to agree.
The eval measures what is STORED: the extractor's output after the quality gate
(extract/worth.rs). The junk-* cases (arithmetic, code, table rows, questions,
filler, fragments) fit a sentence shape without saying anything, and must produce
